name: North Dakota veterans: county and tribal veterans service officers for claims help
organization: North Dakota Department of Veterans Affairs
description: Free help with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits from county veterans service officers in every county and tribal veterans service officers for Fort Berthold, Lake Traverse, Spirit Lake, Standing Rock and Turtle Mountain. The department and the national service officers of AMVETS, the American Legion, DAV and VFW work at the Fargo VA Regional Office.
next_step: Choose a county above for its county veterans service officer. Or call the North Dakota Department of Veterans Affairs at 701-239-7165. National service officers at the Fargo VA Regional Office: American Legion 701-451-4646, DAV 701-451-4636, VFW 701-451-4635.
constraints: Many rural county offices are open only a few days a month; check the hours on the county card and call ahead.

source_evidence.scope: National and state service officers with phones; links to each county and tribal veterans service officer page; read in full.

name: Aging & Disability Resource LINK: North Dakota’s aging and disability line
organization: North Dakota Health and Human Services, Adults and Aging Services
description: The Aging & Disability Resource LINK is the statewide starting point for older adults, adults with disabilities and caregivers: information and referral for help at home, meals, caregiver support, assisted living and other long-term services. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call 855-462-5465 and press 1 for the Resource LINK. TTY users can call 711.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

source_evidence.scope: Toll-free number, TTY, address and the section’s services; read in full.

name: Medicare counseling (State Health Insurance Counseling, SHIC) for North Dakota
organization: North Dakota Insurance Department, State Health Insurance Counseling (SHIC)
description: Free Medicare counseling from North Dakota’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, SHIC, run by the Insurance Department with trained volunteer counselors.
next_step: Call SHIC toll-free at 888-575-6611 (TDD 800-366-6888). For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

source_evidence.title: CMS: Senior Health Insurance Counseling (SHIC), North Dakota
source_evidence.scope: North Dakota Insurance Department, 600 East Boulevard, Bismarck; toll-free (888) 575-6611, TDD (800) 366-6888; search excerpt.

name: North Dakota Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
organization: North Dakota Health and Human Services: Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program; Vulnerable Adult Protective Services
description: Advocacy for people living in nursing homes, basic care, assisted living and swing-bed hospitals. Vulnerable Adult Protective Services takes reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of adults living in the community.
next_step: Call the ombudsman at 701-328-4617, or 855-462-5465 and press 3. To report abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable adult, call 855-462-5465 and press 2 (weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.; messages can be left), or report online. In an emergency, call 911 first.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

name: Free legal help for older North Dakotans
organization: Legal Services of North Dakota; Dakota Plains Legal Services
description: Legal Services of North Dakota gives free civil legal help to low-income and older North Dakotans, with a separate line for callers 60 and older. Dakota Plains Legal Services serves low-income people, older Americans and veterans, including in tribal courts.
next_step: Age 60 and older: call Legal Services of North Dakota at 866-621-9886. Under 60: 800-634-5263.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income and case type.

name: VA health care in North Dakota
organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Fargo VA Health Care System
description: North Dakota veterans are served by the Fargo VA Health Care System: the Fargo VA Medical Center (2101 Elm Street North) and clinics including Bismarck, Grafton, Grand Forks, Jamestown and Minot.
next_step: Call 701-239-3700 or toll-free 800-410-9723. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.

source_evidence.title: VA Fargo health care: Contact us
source_evidence.scope: Mailing address 2101 Elm Street North, Fargo; local 701-239-3700, toll-free 800-410-9723; search excerpt.

source_evidence.title: VA Fargo health care: Locations
source_evidence.scope: Fargo VA Medical Center and clinics in Bismarck, Grafton, Grand Forks, Jamestown and Minot, among others; search excerpt.

name: Dakota Center for Independent Living
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
Main office: 3111 East Broadway Avenue, Bismarck. Toll-free: 800-489-5013. Dickinson office: 26 First Street East, Suite 103, 701-483-4363.

name: Community Action Partnership of North Dakota: veteran housing help (SSVF)
organization: Community Action Partnership of North Dakota
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 12-ND-051): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
